title: Pure-row payoff against the empirical column strategy
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N \ge 1$ column actions, and payoff matrix $A$. Fix a row action $i$ and a sequence of column actions $a_0, \dots, a_{T-1}$ with $T > 0$, and let $\hat{q}$ be the associated empirical column strategy. Then the expected payoff of row $i$ against $\hat{q}$ equals the average payoff over the sequence:
\[
  \sum_{j} A_{ij}\,\hat{q}_j \;=\; \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} A_{i,\,a_t}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: a sequence of T column actions a_0,…,a_{T-1}
q̂ is the empirical strategy of the action sequence
replaced:
For a game $G$, a pure row $i$, and a sequence of pure column actions
$a_0, \dots, a_{T-1}$,
\[
  \mathrm{pureVsPayoff}(G, i, \hat{q})
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} A_{i, a_t},
\]
where $\hat{q}$ is the empirical column strategy.
